fieldNotes.title: Harbor Picnic Clue Page
fieldNotes.useCase: Yard or park walk page for turning safe looking clues into a short harbor scene.
fieldNotes.adultSetup: Print one page, choose a calm outdoor view, and remind the kid to look only and stay with the grown-up.
fieldNotes.kidDirection: Find three broad clues you can see or hear, then pretend one belongs in Spoon Ferry Lunchbox Harbor.
fieldNotes.noticePrompt: I notice a tiny harbor clue: ____________________.
fieldNotes.storySeed: A lunchbox ferry captain finds ____________________ beside the pretend dock.
fieldNotes.revisionNudge: Add one clearer color, size, or sound to the quietest sentence: ____________________.
fieldNotes.quietOptionLine: Quiet version: whisper your detail to the grown-up, then write one word: ____________________.
fieldNotes.takeHomeLine: At home, turn your best outdoor clue into one story sentence: ____________________.

fieldNotes.title: Compass Shop Detail Page
fieldNotes.useCase: Printable walk stop for building a tiny shop setting from broad outdoor details.
fieldNotes.adultSetup: Print the page and choose a safe standing spot with a clear view of sky, ground, plants, or garden edges.
fieldNotes.kidDirection: Look for details that could belong in Penny Path Compass Shop, then write them as setting clues.
fieldNotes.noticePrompt: The compass shop window might show ____________________.
fieldNotes.storySeed: A pocket compass refuses to point until the shopkeeper notices ____________________.
fieldNotes.revisionNudge: Replace one plain word with a sharper outdoor detail: ____________________.
fieldNotes.quietOptionLine: Quiet version: choose one clue silently and write it here: ____________________.
fieldNotes.takeHomeLine: At home, use your compass clue to open a two-sentence story: ____________________.

fieldNotes.title: Greenhouse Gear Pattern Page
fieldNotes.useCase: Adult-guided yard or park page for turning repeated nature details into a story signal.
fieldNotes.adultSetup: Print one page, choose a garden view or porch view, and keep the activity looking only.
fieldNotes.kidDirection: Find something that repeats in shape, color, spacing, or sound, then turn that pattern into a story clue.
fieldNotes.storySeed: A tiny greenhouse machine begins humming when ____________________ repeats three times.
fieldNotes.sentencePath: First the pattern is ____________________, next it changes to ____________________, finally the helper writes ____________________.
fieldNotes.revisionNudge: Add one more pattern detail to the sentence that feels too plain: ____________________.
fieldNotes.quietOptionLine: Quiet version: choose one repeating thing silently and write it: ____________________.
fieldNotes.takeHomeLine: At home, use your pattern as the secret signal in a garden story: ____________________.

fieldNotes.title: Rain Gauge Railway Step Page
fieldNotes.useCase: Printable field note for arranging three outdoor clues into a beginning, middle, and ending.
fieldNotes.adultSetup: Print the page and choose a dry, calm viewing spot after light rain or during a normal outdoor walk.
fieldNotes.kidDirection: Pick three visible clues and pretend each one is a tiny railway stop in order.
fieldNotes.noticePrompt: The first rain-gauge clue I notice is ____________________.
fieldNotes.storySeed: A railway conductor's rain gauge clicks when ____________________ appears beside the track.
fieldNotes.revisionNudge: Add one sound or movement word to the middle step: ____________________.
fieldNotes.quietOptionLine: Quiet version: tap each step on the page, then write the final clue: ____________________.
fieldNotes.takeHomeLine: At home, write a three-step railway scene from broad outdoor clues: ____________________.
